title: a pipeline run's fixed cost is measured stage by stage and cut by infrastructure
desiredOutcome: the tokens and time a pipeline run spends are attributed to stages and to the files each stage reads, by offline tools with tests, and an infrastructure design that cuts the fixed part is chosen on that evidence with its saving predicted and a benchmark that will confirm or refute it

tasks.title: a pipeline run's tokens and time are attributed to stages and files by offline tools with tests
tasks.description:
Measures where a pipeline run spends its tokens and time, with offline tools that have tests and make no paid call. Requested by the user on 2026-10-07 after the feature benchmark showed that the plugin pipeline costs several times more than plain Claude Code on a task both solve.

1. Static context measure. A tool computes what each command and agent loads before it does any work: the command file, every reference file the command instructs the model to read, the agent definition, auto-loaded skills, and the always-on cost (plugin listing, CLAUDE.md). It reports bytes and an estimated token count, labelled as an estimate with its rule. It is computed for the pipeline's real path (/audit:run, /audit:next, /audit:phase, sign-off, executor, reviewer), at the published tag and at local main.

2. Stream attribution. A tool reads a recorded stream-json session and attributes every model request's tokens to a stage: the main loop before any dispatch, plan and manifest work, executor, reviewer, gate, close. It splits each stage into cache write, cache read, input and output, priced with the shipped table. It names the file reads that created the largest cache writes. Run it on the recorded plugin sessions: the pipeline pilot, and the plugin arm of the feature benchmark under the internal analysis directory's experiments. Report what each stage cost in each.

3. Tests. Each tool has a selftest that meets the repository's contract, with fixtures. Attribution is proved on a hand-built stream whose answer is known, including a twin that must not move a token between stages.

4. docs/research/pipeline-cost-analysis.md states, from these measurements:
- which part of a run's cost is fixed per run, per task, and per file the work touches;
- what the prompt cache already saves and what it cannot;
- the largest single contributors.
Every figure sits beside the command that re-derives it.

outcome.technical: tools/stream-cost.py attributes every request of a recorded stream-json session to a stage: orient, plan, executor, gate, reviewer, close, or main for a session that dispatches nothing. It reports each stage's cache write, cache read, input and output, priced through _usage_core.price. A second view attributes cost by content origin, using exact read counts from the cached-prefix identity: the session start, each reference file read, agent starts, briefs, hand-backs and the files the work touches, classed as fixed per run, per task or per file. Each subagent's final request, which the stream omits, is rebuilt from the modelUsage residual, and the tool labels any estimate. tools/measure-context.py computes what each command and agent loads before working: the up-front read paragraphs, the agent prompt and preloaded skills, and the always-on listing, at any git ref, in bytes and in calibrated tokens. docs/research/pipeline-cost-analysis.md explains both published observations with figures re-derived by these commands. In the pilot, the reference prose /audit:run names is written into the cache once and carried on every later main-loop request, and that is the largest share of the run. In the plugin arm of the feature benchmark against the plain arm, the per-file cost is about equal; the gap is the run class (reference prose) and the task class (agent starts written fresh, briefs, hand-backs). The document reports what the cache saves and cannot save, the largest contributors, the measured bytes-per-token of the prose, and the prose growth from v3.1.0 to main. gate-parity gains one NOT_AN_EXEMPTION row for the tool's legend table. The red-first helper could not run because the task declares no separate test file. Instead, scratch-copy mutations of both tools each turned their intended case red: sc1-sc21 and mc1-mc12, with over-fire twins. Every tool output was regenerated after a gap and was byte-identical.
outcome.descriptive: Two new offline tools show exactly where a plugin run spends its tokens - the reference documents read up front and the fresh start of each agent - and that the coding work itself costs about the same with or without the plugin.

verifiedBy: mc1-mc12; tools/stream-cost.py and measure-context.py over the four recorded sessions

intentCheck.basis: orchestrator check: both published observations explained with re-derivable figures, tools reproduce the CLI's costUSD per model, mutations proved every case, run at Opus 5.5 xhigh as the user asked
